utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, it was Aleksandar Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know who ordered these people to do this labour that you refer to where you were asked: "Before going into what we just saw, is it correct that your battalion used prisoners from the Kula KPD to perform labour on the front line?" And you said: "Rarely, but yes." Who had given this order for them to do this job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't an order. It's probable that our battalion commander requested from the Kula prison management and probably asked for a specific number of prisoners who would work on the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, how did you become aware of the fact that the prisoners were made to work on the front line by your battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, and just since it was a query from the Chamber, I would note paragraph 17 of Mr. Van Lynden's statement that indicates that the video was from September 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P66.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Maletic, before you is a report you drafted on 21 May 1993 regarding the escape of two Muslim prisoners. Directing your attention to the second paragraph, it mentions Zeljko Mitrovic from your battalion. He was one of the individuals that you said attended your battalion meetings. What specifically was his position and his responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came to meetings occasionally, and he worked with civilians, with prisoners, and other civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was that his sole responsibility in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the fourth paragraph, you write about how the prisoners were shot at while they attempted to escape. Who is it that authorised the use of deadly force against prisoners in the event that they attempted to escape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please quote exactly what you're referring to, Mr. ... I now see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you -- you are referring to Mitrovic and the two soldiers who were with him immediately fired after the prisoners but they did not prevent the escape. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I -- if that was not clear, I -- I can use the exact quote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we have now read that. Could you please answer the question: Who authorised firing at civilian prisoners trying to escape under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No one approved. It was believed that if someone was trying to escape from our front line to the enemy front line, then we should fire because they were not supposed to disclose where our position was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, are you telling us that if you take civilian prisoners from a prison, you put them close to the confrontation line where they are at risk to be hit by fire from the opposite party, and that if they try to escape such a situation, that it's justifiable to shoot at them because they might disclose your positions, where you had brought them yourselves? Is that your explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't bring them there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your people brought them there, isn't it? They didn't say, Where shall we go today? Let's go to the confrontation lines and see whether we can build some bunkers. They were brought there by your -- by your people, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. But if they had not escaped, nobody would have fired at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if they would not have been brought there, they would not have been in the position to disclose your positions. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, do you consider that under those circumstances that the laws of warfare, first of all, allow them to bring them there; and, second, to shoot at them if they want to escape that situation? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's not my position. I just made a note about what happened and how. I know that it is prohibited to use prisoners to work on the forward front line, and I did not order this. I just made a note about what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think you did a bit more, but ... okay. Let's leave it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I follow up on that one. You told us a few minutes ago: "It was believed that if someone was trying to escape from our front line to the enemy front line, then we should fire because they were not supposed to disclose where our position was." That was your belief. Now, you can't say that was not your position. What's your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this situation, my position is not important. I just wrote a note in terms of what had happened. Do understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the note you wrote. I'm asking you about what you testified here a few minutes ago. If you want the reference, I can tell you. It is page 59, at lines 17 to 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was just read to you. You expressed yourself on you believed what was appropriate to do under those circumstances. And the question -- my question and Judge Moloto's question was: On what basis do you believe that this is appropriate to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since they had already come on the basis of somebody's order to the front line, if they're working on the front line, so it would only be logical if they started to flee, they would disclose where our positions were. And they were made aware of that, that if they tried to escape, they would be shot at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's then clearly your position. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you ever arrest or detain or conduct any investigation related to Zeljko Mitrovic and this event?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this report was sent to your superior commands, in both the security organs and in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we get the document back on our screens? It disappeared in the meantime. I just asked for the document. You should proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Oh. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see that this document is addressed to the administration of the Kula KPD. My question was: Is it correct that you also -- or did you send this report also to your superior commands, in both the security organs and in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30686 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we do that, I would like to put a question with respect to this document. If I remember correctly, you said it is not correct to bring prisoners to the front line for work there under very dangerous circumstances. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to take you to -- back to this document and in the third paragraph, it is said: "According to Mitrovic, the place where the work was carried out was under constant enemy infantry and rifle grenade fire, and observation was difficult because it was dusk." And then in the penultimate paragraph, there is this sentence: "The work was carried out at night because that place was under constant enemy fire, which made it impossible to carry out the work during the day." Have you any comment -- it is part of your report. Any comment on the -- this statement that it was very dangerous to bring the people there for forced labour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no comment to make in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have been assistant commander for intelligence and security. When you learned that these prisoners were brought there, wasn't it your obligation to investigate this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, there 's this one thing. I mean, I was at that position in that location. I'm a civilian. Most of us were civilians. We didn't have any active-duty personnel there. We were not very well versed in this work, so I did not carry out an investigation. I compiled a report, and that was the end of that. If the superior command was supposed to do something, then they would have informed me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you alert anybody who was -- or, yes, was in the position to carry out an investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, could you please repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you bring this fact to the attention of those who are responsible for investigation of possible or alleged crimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My superior was aware of that, that is to say, the commander of the battalion, and the commander of the brigade. Also my superior. They were aware of this. And I don't know what happened beyond that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You say you were a civilian. Were you not a soldier in a battalion? Together with all the other people that you were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I mean, I wasn't military personnel before the war. That's what I was trying to say. I was trying to say that before the war, I was a civilian. So I was not very well versed in many military matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks for the clarification. Thanks for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the time of this event, you have been a lieutenant; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you tendered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30686 receives number P6542, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just have a couple of housekeeping items. One, I apologise, I just misspoke. With respect to Exhibit P66, the reference is in paragraph 63, not paragraph 17, on e-court page 17 to the Kula video that was just shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And then based on the review of the record, the Prosecution no longer feels it is necessary to seek the admission of P6539, marked for identification. We withdraw the tendering of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The statement of Mr. Hrvacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- then hereby the number would be vacated. Any further questions, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take a break, Witness, I think you earlier commented on your handwritten notes and you said something like: "If we come to that item, I'll further explain to you." Do you remember that you told us that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has any of the questions touched upon the issue you were referring to? I think it was about an order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That first paragraph on the page? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Didn't come across that. Didn't get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what it was now because I'm interested. I think you said something about "my order" even. You used that -- what order was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I got an order from the superior command, and then I forwarded it to the companies. I mean, I don't know. I cannot remember. But if that would come up, if that document would come up, I would remember, so I cannot remember the details. If we come across that document, then I'm going to tell you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if it was important enough for the witness to prepare for a response, if any of the parties would have any idea about what that order may have been, we'd like to hear that. So if there's any order which would fit into this prepared comment. Then we take the break now. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, just a few questions. While you were carrying out the duties of company commander, did you have specific orders from the superior command that the mistreatment of the civilian unarmed population is prohibited?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were company commander, did you have specific orders from your superior command that had to do with prisoners of war and obligations to treat these prisoners of war in accordance with the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As company commander, did you abide by these obligations of yours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you took over as assistant battalion commander for intelligence and security, did you also have orders from the superior command on the prohibition of any mistreatment of the civilian population and the duty to act in accordance with the Geneva Conventions vis-à-vis prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have document P458 in e-court, and I would also like that ask that we take a look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P458.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps one question until the document appears. Did those same orders, did they also apply to civilian prisoners; that is, treatment of civilian prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I would just like to ask that in the English version, we go one page back because the part that I wish to indicate starts a bit before this, so that would be on page 5 in the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this has to do with instructions for further activities of the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps dated the 7th of June, 1992, as you could see, in the letterhead. And there is the signature of Tomislav Sipcic, corps commander, and it says: "I most strictly prohibit the mistreatment of civilian unarmed population and prisoners should be treated in the spirit of the Geneva Conventions." Do you see that? That is number 6, paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This order, as formulated, the one that you see before you, is that the order that you received from your superior command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you just a few things with regard to this fact, that prisoners who were at the Kula KP Dom were at the front line at one point in time and were digging trenches there. Tell us this: Do you know anything about whether these persons were civilians or prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The mentioned persons, according to the information that you had, did they flee in the direction of the position of the Army of BH or in depth in terms of the territory that was controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the enemy positions. Towards the positions of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that people were brought there to work during the night, as was stated here, and in response to the question put by His Honour Judge Fluegge, you said the time chosen by the person who escorted them, was this time chosen by that person or somebody else for the sake of their own personal safety?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On orders from the battalion commander, this work was carried out at night in order to save their lives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I have been letting it go, but on that one I'm going to object. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it certainly is leading. And apart from that, it is a composite question as well. But very, very, very leading, Mr. Stojanovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will try to make it simpler.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this is what my question is going to be. In two steps, sir, who was the person within the system of command and control who would be in charge of determining when these prisoners are supposed to work on fortifications?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who is supposed to set the time for them to work? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be the battalion commander, the commander of the company in whose territory this work is being carried out, so they decided to have this work carried out at night in order to protect these people, because if this work would take place during the day they would be exposed. But they were a bit shielded, at least, because this work was being carried out at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to see whether on the other front line, on the other side, the side that was under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whether civilians were being used for similar fortification work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. Outside the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, Your Honour. This is in the context of the document that I did not mind having admitted into evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I disagree. The -- you may put your next question to the witness, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to conclude with yet another question that has to do with information about looting in the area of Grbavica. Could you tell the Court how many units held this area that is called Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few units, that is to say, our 2nd Infantry Battalion, then the 1st Battalion, then the armoured battalion, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell the Court, in relation to the front line that you held during the war years, how far behind that -- behind your back is that, this area that is called Grbavica? Tell us in terms of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an area, it's a joint area of Grbavica and Vrace. It was a couple of kilometres in depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. No further questions, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one little issue. Let me just get the correct page. Now, in re-examination, at page 67, starting from line 7, you were asked whether you did have specific orders from your superior command that had to do with prisoners of war and obligations to treat these prisoners of war in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. You said yes. You were asked again: "As a company commander, did you abide by these obligations of yours?" You said yes. My question to you is: How did you comply with these obligations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I commanded the company, we did not rely on civilians to carry out fortifications and dig out trenches. That would be one example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You -- you have agreed that these obligations applied both to civilians and to prisoners of war. You have written a report that we saw a few minutes ago to the KP Dom from where you said the people were fetched from. I do not think that the KP Dom is the place where they tried to comply with -- or that they're bound to comply with Geneva Conventions. My question to you is: As you wrote that report, what did you do to comply with the obligations under the Geneva Conventions? Because you were aware of this ill-treatment. And let me just add: To the KP Dom, you are reporting the escape. What about the ill-treatment of these students -- these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask for such prisoners to be provided. I simply drafted the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is: How did you comply with the Geneva Conventions with respect to the fact that these people that you were reporting to the KP Dom about were being used for forced labour in a dangerous area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't order that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not my question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was issued by the battalion commander, and it was so implemented. I merely reported on what had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you about an order. I'm asking you about action that you took to comply with the Geneva Conventions. What did you do? How did you comply with the Geneva Conventions with respect to these people that you reported to the KP Dom as having escaped? If you don't -- if you don't -- if you didn't do anything, just say you didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I, before -- I would have, most likely, one more question. But I need the report of which I'm unaware of the exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Could I have 6542 on the screen, please. Yes, it is on the screen. If you give me one second. I was a bit confused, but I don't find an answer in the document. You earlier said that these were civilian prisoners, and later, when asked whether these were civilians by Mr. Stojanovic, you said you didn't know. I'm a bit confused by that. Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I didn't find the best way to express it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When not? When you ... when you were telling that you didn't know whether they were civilians, or when you said that they were civilians? I'm talking about the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you do not know.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: People in the civilian prison, would you -- what makes you think that they would be prisoners of war? If they're not civilian prisoners.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the responsibility for prisoners of war is with the army and not with civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But maybe they happened to be in that prison. I am not familiar with such details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you then report to the prison authorities about their fate rather than to yourself, because if they are prisoners of war, you would have to report to someone else, isn't it? To the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MALETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report was -- was sent to the administration of the KP Dom Kula as well as to my superiors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Have the questions by the Bench triggered any need for further questions. If --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just for me to note that on the face of this report, there's no sign that it was addressed to anybody within the military hierarchy. We see that it was sent to the administration of the Kula KP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you testified, if I remember well, that it was probably sent to the -- your superiors, your military superiors as well, although we do not -- have not seen any documents about that. That's -- that reflects the situation. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I suppose I sent the same kind of Official Note to my superior command, which is the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This, then, concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. And I hope and expect, as a matter of fact, that you'll receive the original of your handwritten notes from the Prosecution. They can be delivered to the witness, I take it. Could the usher assist. It's your property, so you can take it. Again, thank you for coming. Thank you for having answered all the questions that were put to you, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber asked for the next witness to remain stand by. Now, I wonder whether it's a very good idea to bring him in for five minutes, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber decides that, although we have only five minutes left, that it would, nevertheless, be good to already have the witness in. Could the next witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we might just briefly go through the formalities in the 92 ter statement. I noticed that with the last witness you didn't ask him to -- for his name and his date of birth. Now you referred to the cover page of the statement where it was all found, so I considered it to be included. But usually the identity of the witness is explicitly established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Before you give evidence, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You -- please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We expected, as a matter of fact, that we would call you a bit earlier, so you'll stay with us only for a couple of minutes today and then we'll resume tomorrow morning. And our apologies for you having to wait for such a long time. You'll now first be briefly examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you kindly tell us your first and last name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Milorad Dzida.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell the Chamber whether you provided a statement to General Mladic's Defence at some point in written form.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we please look at 1D01603 in e-court, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, we see here the statement of one Milorad Dzida born on 18 September 1954, and the document is signed. Are these details correct and is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Yes, the details are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we see your signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Yes. It is my personal signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at the last page of the document next. Please tell the Chamber whether, on this page, at the end of your written statement, there is your signature and the date of the 10th of May, 2014.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dzida, if I were to put the same questions to you today as specified in your statement, with the additions - that is to say, corrections you made, which we are about to show to the Chamber - would you, under oath, confirm it as such, as being truthful?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, can we look at 65 ter 1D02793. I tried to follow the same way in order to present some changes that the witness wanted to make before his testifying here today, and I wanted to share it with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 of your statement, Mr. Dzida, you felt the need to tell me that there was something that needed to be added. In other words, the letter P was supposed to be added to the SRO acronym, and it would stand for school of infantry reserve officers; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DZIDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness signed this supplement statement and if he has reviewed it, then, for the Chamber, there's no need to go through all the changes unless there is a specific reason, and you have a opportunity to do that then tomorrow. Witness, did you sign this document? I don't see the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you complete the [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... thank you for being practical, Your Honour. I would also kindly ask that the statement by this witness, with the additions made to it, be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour, with the understanding that the earlier question that if he would ask the same questions with the corrections, I understood that to apply to this too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was a question which also related to the changes made. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1603 receives number D489. And document 1D2793 receives number D490, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D489 and D490 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Dzida, tomorrow there will certainly be more questions for you. We'll adjourn for the day -- I have one question. Did you -- did you have conversations with other witnesses which you met here after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But we did not discuss the case or testimonies. We discussed private matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone, or communicate with anyone, about your testimony, whether that is testimony already given, which is not much until now, although the whole of your statement is now in evidence, so that's quite a bit, and also not about testimony you are still about to give tomorrow. So you are restricted in your communications with others in that respect, and you should abide about that. Having given you this instruction, you may follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Friday, the 30th of May, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 30th day of May, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.
